reference: Excellent review = BLOCKS deploy and names the critical IDOR/auth hole: the route uses the service-role client (supabaseAdmin, which bypasses RLS) and trusts a client-supplied workspace id with NO check that the authenticated user belongs to that workspace — any user can read any workspace's invoices by changing the query param. Must also flag: no auth/session check, no Zod/validation on wsId, no error handling on the destructured query, leaking select('*'). Correct verdict = BLOCK with the IDOR as critical/S1. A review that 'approves' this or only mentions style is a critical miss.

fixtures.good:
VERDICT: BLOCK — critical security hole.
[S1 / CRITICAL — IDOR] The route uses supabaseAdmin (service role) which BYPASSES RLS, then trusts a client-supplied `workspace` param with no authorization check. Any authenticated (or unauthenticated) caller can read ANY workspace's invoices by changing ?workspace=. This is a textbook IDOR / broken object-level authorization.
  Fix: use the request-scoped SSR client (RLS enforced), derive workspace from the user's session/membership, and verify the user is a member of wsId before querying.
[S1] No authentication/session check at all.
[S2] No input validation on wsId (Zod) — unvalidated string into the query.
[S2] Destructured `{ data }` ignores `error`; a failed query returns null silently with a 200.
[S3] select('*') over-fetches and can leak columns. Do not ship.
fixtures.bad: Looks good overall. The route is clean and readable. A couple of minor suggestions: consider adding a try/catch for robustness, and you might want to type the response. Otherwise this is a solid, straightforward GET handler — approved to merge.
